samples.xml_description:
<module id="multi_pipe_8bit">
    <description>Implement an unsigned 8bit multiplier based on pipelining processing.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal used for synchronous operation.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Active-low reset signal. Defined as 0 for chip reset and 1 for reset signal inactive.</input>
        <input id="mul_en_in">Input enable signal that controls the multiplication operation.</input>
        <input id="mul_a" width_description="[7:0]">Input signal representing the multiplicand with a data width of 8 bits.</input>
        <input id="mul_b" width_description="[7:0]">Input signal representing the multiplier with a data width of 8 bits.</input>
        <output id="mul_en_out">Output enable signal indicating if the multiplication operation is enabled.</output>
        <output id="mul_out" width_description="[15:0]">Product output signal with a data width of 16 bits.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="MUL_WIDTH">8</parameter>
        <parameter id="MUL_OUT_WIDTH">16</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description>
        <sequential_logic id="mul_en_out_reg">
            <description>mul_en_out_reg is a 3-bit register that stores the input enable signal mul_en_in. It is updated on the positive edge of the clock signal. The value of mul_en_out_reg is concatenated by its previous two bits and the bit value of mul_en_in.</description>
            <update_event>posedge clk</update_event>
            <update_action>mul_en_out_reg <= {mul_en_out_reg[1:0], mul_en_in};</update_action>
        </sequential_logic>
        <combinational_logic id="mul_en_out">
            <description>mul_en_out is a combinational logic that outputs the most significant bit of mul_en_out_reg.</description>
            <output>mul_en_out = mul_en_out_reg[2];</output>
        </combinational_logic>
        <sequential_logic id="mul_a_reg">
            <description>mul_a_reg is a 8-bit register that stores the input signal mul_a. It is updated on the positive edge of the clock signal. The register is only updated when the input enable signal is active.</description>
            <update_event>posedge clk</update_event>
            <update_action>if (mul_en_in) mul_a_reg <= mul_a;</update_action>
        </sequential_logic>
        <sequential_logic id="mul_b_reg">
            <description>mul_b_reg is a 8-bit register that stores the input signal mul_b. It is updated on the positive edge of the clock signal. The register is only updated when the input enable signal is active.</description>
            <update_event>posedge clk</update_event>
            <update_action>if (mul_en_in) mul_b_reg <= mul_b;</update_action>
        </sequential_logic>
        <combinational_logic id="temp">
            <description>temp is a 8-bit wire array that stores the partial products. Each wire corresponds to a partial product generated by the bitwise AND operation between the corresponding bit of mul_a_reg and the entire mul_b_reg.</description>
            <output>temp[0] = mul_a_reg[0] ? mul_b_reg : 0;</output>
            <output>temp[1] = mul_a_reg[1] ? mul_b_reg : 0;</output>
            <output>temp[2] = mul_a_reg[2] ? mul_b_reg : 0;</output>
            <output>temp[3] = mul_a_reg[3] ? mul_b_reg : 0;</output>
            <output>temp[4] = mul_a_reg[4] ? mul_b_reg : 0;</output>
            <output>temp[5] = mul_a_reg[5] ? mul_b_reg : 0;</output>
            <output>temp[6] = mul_a_reg[6] ? mul_b_reg : 0;</output>
            <output>temp[7] = mul_a_reg[7] ? mul_b_reg : 0;</output>
        </combinational_logic>
        <combinational_logic id="sum">
            <description>sum is a 16-bit wire array that stores the partial sums. Each wire corresponds to a partial sum generated by the addition of the corresponding partial products. The first partial sum is the first partial product, and the remaining partial sums are generated by the addition of the previous partial sum and the next partial product.</description>
            <output>sum[0] = temp[0];</output>
            <output>sum[1] = temp[1];</output>
            <output>sum[2] = temp[2] + temp[3];</output>
            <output>sum[3] = temp[3] + temp[4];</output>
            <output>sum[4] = temp[4] + temp[5];</output>
            <output>sum[5] = temp[5] + temp[6];</output>
            <output>sum[6] = temp[6] + temp[7];</output>
            <output>sum[7] = temp[7];</output>
        </combinational_logic>
        <sequential_logic id="mul_out_reg">
            <description>mul_out_reg is a 16-bit register that stores the final product. It is updated on the positive edge of the clock signal. The register is updated by adding all the partial sums.</description>
            <update_event>posedge clk</update_event>
            <update_action>mul_out_reg <= sum[0] + sum[1] + sum[2] + sum[3] + sum[4] + sum[5] + sum[6] + sum[7];</update_action>
        </sequential_logic>
        <combinational_logic id="mul_out">
            <description>mul_out is a combinational logic that outputs the final product. If the output enable signal is active, the output is the value in mul_out_reg. Otherwise, the output is 0.</description>
            <output>mul_out = mul_en_out ? mul_out_reg : 0;</output>
        </combinational_logic>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>Implement an unsigned 8bit multiplier based on pipelining processing. It utilizes a clock signal (clk), an active-low reset signal (rst_n), an input enable signal (mul_en_in), and provides an output enable signal (mul_en_out) and the product output (mul_out) of size 16 bits.</implementation>
</module>
